description: P3 consumer-assertion + live-constant pin for CHECK 14 (no turn-terminating language in sub-step skill body prose, issue #321). A skill body loads into its CALLING AGENT's context, so caller-scoped terminal prose makes an agent that invokes the skill inline end its turn early and return the skill's output as its own — a silent false PASS. The set_check pins the DETECTION CONSTANTS AS THEY LIVE IN tools/policy_check.sh: it captures the single-quoted RHS body of every line-anchored CHECK14_(TERMINAL|KEEP|TOKEN)_REGEX assignment in the check itself and asserts set EQUALITY, not membership. Equality is what closes the class: a MISSING member fails (deleting a terminal alternative, dropping the `^Emit exactly` anchor, weakening the `stop-and-merge` KEEP phrase, or loosening the token regex's namespace/charset), and an EXTRA member fails too (a shadowing later reassignment that leaves the pinned assignment as dead text can no longer smuggle a weakened live value past the pin). It pins the three live regex constants only — it does not assert the check's runtime behaviour on any sample body, and the non-regex CHECK14_SKILLTOOL_MARKER is pinned by full-literal consumer instead. The consumers pin the load-bearing literals proving the check exists and keeps its contract: the `=== CHECK 14:` section header, `add_finding 'CHECK14'` (it emits CHECK14 findings), the caller-derived discovery that excludes overlord.md, the two position-free discovery constants (Skill-tool marker literal, token regex assignment name), and the three fail-closed findings — empty derived set, marked-but-unresolvable line, and mention/token parity failure.

expected_set: Your final action|final action is a|[Pp]roduce zero (text|chat)|^Emit exactly|and stop
